item.title: Fox/litter/junk food mural, 14th August
item.description:
Without taking anything away from the obvious talent and good intentions of the artist, this typifies some of the local street art which is arguably not enhancing but the opposite. Surely more inspiring and pleasing images could be considered that don't evoke outdoor pests, litter and junk food as if this wasn't already an issue in the area. While others may well feel differently, I believe residents should have been consulted and ideally would have an opportunity to feedback on it.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): High Street, Anerley, Greater London

item.title: 2 very tall trees need pruning hanging over Parkside Close, 14th August
item.description:
I am writing to report two trees located within Penge Recreation Ground which appear to be hanging/overhanging onto Parkside Close, Penge. The branches extend over the boundary towards the private properties in Parkside Close and are causing concern regarding safety, access and potential damage to property. Could you please arrange for the trees to be inspected by the appropriate Council tree officer or arboricultural team and advise whether any pruning or other maintenance is required? I would be grateful if you could confirm that this report has been received and provide a reference number Kind regards, Mrs Jennie Phillips

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Parkside Close, Penge, Greater London

item.title: Low Trees affecting my parking and leaving house on windy days, 14th August
item.description:
The tree outside 75 is beautiful, and surely protected with a TPO.. however has grown so large and low to the ground, the branches can touch and scratch the top of my 2026 Disability lease car. On a windy day I am afraid to leave my house as it is such a large tree with many branches falling to the ground, and hard, spiky conker like pods, reaching over my car and front garden/ path. I have lived here for 29 years and never seen this tree so big. I’m sure it has not been trimmed in years, but the tree next to it was trimmed a few weeks back. Hopefully this tree is next, before the winter sets in. I need to few safe leaving my house and getting into my car, as I have mobility issues. The tree roots have also caused havoc pulling up the pavement, which needs attention; grown into my drains and up my front path all the way to my front door. Which my landlord has taken care of.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Station Road, Crayford, Greater London
